messages:
incident-bot: Pager: GPU scheduling pressure detected on inference-cluster-east. Queues growing > 3k, throttled requests increasing. Severity: SEV2. Auto-scaler attempted scale but hit max_nodes limit.
Alex Chen: seeing massive request backlog on text-gen routes, right? numbers?
Sara Patel: queue ~= 3.9k, throttled ~2.2k; GPU utilization at 94% cluster-wide, but available GPU slices reported ~18% stranded due to MIG fragmentation.
Ryan O'Neill: confirmed. autoscaler shows desired_nodes=70, current_nodes=50, max_nodes=50 (policy). Tried a scale request, got capped.
Nina (oncall): I'm taking lead. Immediate question: any customer-facing errors yet?
Jane Park: acme-corp dedicated pool is experiencing elevated latencies and 429s. Support ticket #INC-7842 flagged.
Mike Li: internal metrics show small MIG slices (1g) pinned to many low-memory models; large-model traffic needs 7g-equivalent; mismatch causing binpack gaps.
Alex Chen: so fragmentation: we have free GPU memory in many small slices but can't fit large-variant models -> stranded capacity.
ops-bot: Alert: autoscaler rejected provision request (reason: max_nodes_reached). Current cloud quota available but cluster config prohibits scale.
Sara Patel: short-term mitigation: 1) route some traffic to smaller lightweight model variant, 2) relax autoscaler max_nodes to 80, 3) manually drain and replace few heterogeneous nodes with nodes using larger MIG profile. Thoughts?
Ryan O'Neill: agree. Routing change is fastest. I'll update router policy to send non-SLA routes to small-variant for next 15m.
Alex Chen: how risky is increasing max_nodes? Any org approval needed?
Nina (oncall): ops quota shows room; I'll push a temporary override for autoscaler max from 50->80 for this cluster. Doing now.
incident-bot: Autoscaler override applied by Nina. New max_nodes=80.
Mike Li: lifecycle note: changing cluster MIG partitioning requires node replacement. We can't resize live. We'll need to cordon/drain specific nodes that hold many small MIGs and spin up instances with the 7g-style MIG profile.
Jane Park: I'll draft a short customer message for acme-corp and attach mitigation steps. Minimal SLA impact for other customers but acme is on dedicated 7g-variant.
Sara Patel: I'll start a rolling drain plan. Target nodes: gpu-node-22, gpu-node-23, gpu-node-24 have high fragmentation. Plan: cordon -> drain -> terminate -> replacement with nodes provisioned using 7g partition template.
Ryan O'Neill: running commands now:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-22
kubectl drain gpu-node-22 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
# confirm workloads moved
```
Alex Chen: watch for stuck pods with local state. If can't evict, we'll scale down affected model replicas manually then restart.
Nina (oncall): autoscaler is already launching new nodes, we have +12 in provisioning. Tracking provisioning latency ~ 90-120s per instance.
incident-bot: Metric update: queue length down to 2.4k after router change and initial scale activity. Throttles down to ~800.
Mike Li: good signal. Still seeing some tail latency for acme-corp. If drain doesn't finish quick, consider temporary CPU fallback for non-critical batches (degraded quality acceptable) to free up GPU cycles.
Sara Patel: I'm on a short handoff in 20m. Ryan, can you take over coordination if I'm paged?
Ryan O'Neill: I can. I'll monitor drain progress and the replacement nodes' MIG profile.
Jane Park: customer update drafted and sent to acme-corp: "We're actively mitigating an infrastructure scheduling issue affecting your dedicated model pool. We're performing targeted node replacement and expect recovery within 45-60 minutes. We'll follow up with post-incident analysis"
Alex Chen: logs showing scheduler rebind errors occasionally: "failed to place pod: insufficient [gpu-7g] resources" — confirms packing mismatch.
ops-bot: Cloud provider reports some spot pools delayed; two replacement instances pending longer than expected.
Nina (oncall): I'm escalating to infra procurement to move some replacements to ondemand to speed up recovery.
incident-bot: Update: queue 1.1k, throttles 320, GPU util 88%, stranded capacity estimate ~12% (down from 18%).
Mike Li: good. Once we have enough compatible 7g nodes, we'll rebalance; that should eliminate the stranded slices. Postmortem action: evaluate better MIG packing heuristics and add autoscaler policy that can increase max temporarily on fragmentation detection.
Sara Patel: quick note before handoff: handoff to Ryan at 2129991145. Primary next steps: finish node replacement (target 8 nodes), verify routing rollback conditions (queue < 300 and throttles < 50 for 10m), and prepare follow-up with capacity engineering for MIG rebalancing automation.
Ryan O'Neill: taking over. I'll post updates here.
Alex Chen: thx team. After this stabilizes, we should run a cluster simulation for mixed-model traffic to stress-test MIG profiles.
Jane Park: posted incident ack to support channel and updated INC-7842 timeline.
incident-bot: Incident status: Mitigated (partial). Monitoring.
Sara Patel: leaving meeting. back in ~2h.
Ryan O'Neill: noted. continuing watch. will PM when fully recovered.
